hints: Use $v = u + at$ with $u = 0$, $v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and $t = 5\text{ s}$ to find the acceleration down the plane.
Apply Newton's second law down the $20^\circ$ inclined plane: $mg\sin 20^\circ - F = ma$.
Substitute $m = 0.1\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and your calculated acceleration to find the friction force $F$.
walkthrough:
The particle starts from rest ($u = 0$) and reaches speed $v = 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$ in $t = 5\text{ s}$. The SUVAT formula is:
$$v = u + at$$
$$2 = 0 + 5a \implies a = \frac{2}{5} = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Next, resolve forces acting on the $0.1\text{ kg}$ particle along the incline. Gravity exerts a downward component $mg\sin 20^\circ$, while friction $F$ opposes the downward motion:
$$F_{\text{net}} = mg\sin 20^\circ - F$$

By Newton's second law, $F_{\text{net}} = ma$:
$$mg\sin 20^\circ - F = ma$$

Substitute $m = 0.1\text{ kg}$, $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$, and $a = 0.4\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$0.1 \times 10 \times \sin 20^\circ - F = 0.1 \times 0.4$$
$$1.0\sin 20^\circ - F = 0.04$$

hints: Resolve forces perpendicular to the incline to find the normal reaction: $R = mg\cos 20^\circ$.
Use the friction relationship $\mu = \frac{F}{R}$ with the friction force $F = 0.30202\text{ N}$ found in part (i).
walkthrough:
Because there is no motion perpendicular to the plane, the normal reaction $R$ balances the perpendicular component of weight:
$$R = mg\cos\theta = 0.1 \times 10 \times \cos 20^\circ = \cos 20^\circ$$
$$R \approx 0.93969\text{ N}$$

The particle is sliding, so limiting friction applies: $F = \mu R$. Rearrange to solve for $\mu$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R}$$

Substitute the unrounded frictional force $F = 0.30202\text{ N}$ and normal reaction $R = 0.93969\text{ N}$:
$$\mu = \frac{0.30202}{0.93969} \approx 0.3214 \approx 0.321$$
